title: Foundations

objectives.text: Place common protocols on the OSI and TCP/IP layers
Describe the TCP handshake and the job of each TCP flag, and contrast TCP with UDP
Recall the common service ports and compute subnet sizes and ranges
Explain what DNS, DHCP, ARP and HTTP do and why each can be abused
Read and set Linux permissions, including SUID, SGID and the sticky bit
Use core Linux and Windows commands to list users, privileges, processes and listening ports
Apply CIA, AAA and risk vocabulary to short scenarios
Classify security controls by type and by function
Build an isolated lab with Kali and a vulnerable VM, and state the legal limits of practice

labs.name: Home lab: Kali + Metasploitable 2 on a host-only network
labs.skill: Building an isolated lab, taking snapshots, a first ping and nmap from Kali

labs.name: OverTheWire Bandit, levels 0–10
labs.skill: Linux command line: files, permissions, find, grep, SSH

labs.name: TryHackMe Pre Security path (free rooms)
labs.skill: Networking basics, how the web works, Linux and Windows fundamentals

labs.name: Wireshark: capture a TCP handshake and a DNS lookup
labs.skill: Seeing SYN, SYN/ACK, ACK and a UDP DNS query on the wire

feynmanPrompts: Explain what happens, packet by packet, when your browser opens https://example.org: DNS, the TCP handshake, then TLS and HTTP.
Explain why a root-owned SUID program is dangerous, and how you would find such programs.
Explain the difference between authentication and authorization with an example from your own life, then say which control types apply.
